what: built_at was stamped at the end of rebuild, so a record rewritten mid-rebuild read as not stale.
how: Reproduced. built_at now stores t0 (taken before the first read), so anything written after the rebuild began compares as newer.

what: --write landed a library-wide degenerate roster over the good one when ONOMASTICON / CONTINUITY_GROUPS were unread, rc 0.
how: main() --write now refuses (rc 1, stderr, nothing written) unless LAST_BUILD onomasticon and continuity_groups are both 'ok' ('partial' refuses too; the live ONOMASTICON has 0 bad rows).

what: sweep.py and worldseed --write built a whole-library file from pipeline.records(), which drops unreadable records silently.
how: Added corpus_db.unreadable_records() (parses every data/records/*.json, names each failure, uncapped). sweep.main() and worldseed --write ask it first and refuse rc 1 with nothing written. It is checked in the write paths only, so existing stubs of sweep() and build_all() are unaffected. pipeline.records() is not mine and is unchanged.

what: A re-extract left the old resume cursor, so a re-supplied book was skipped or reported complete with 0 entries.
how: extract() hashes pages.json before and after landing; if the corpus bytes changed and ingest_state.json exists, the cursor is moved to ingest_state.json.superseded-<ts> (archived, not deleted; a failed move raises OSError which main() reports as a refusal). Re-extracting identical text keeps the cursor. Covers legacy cursors, which carry no digest.

what: crag, nation, capital/jewel/golden and engine stems tagged whole words (Cragmaw, Goldenrod, Capitalist, Engineer) as attested features.
how: Those four table entries now list suffixes or whole words, as sweep67 ruling 4c7cf744461d did for the short stems; genuine mountains, capital and engine still attest.

what: _land_halt overwrote a persistently corrupt HALT.json with the stand-in, destroying the original halt's reason.
how: When the read is the fail-closed stand-in, the unreadable file is first copied to HALT.json.unreadable-<ns> and named in 'preserved_as'; the 'unreadable' flag is dropped from the landed payload. If the copy fails the attempt is refused (the corrupt file still holds the library halted, so fail-closed is kept and the caller's loud path reports it). No halt is ever lifted or weakened.

what: pause() accepted zero (indefinite) and negative (already expired) hours.
how: hours is tested against None and must be finite and > 0, else ValueError (the CLI already catches it and returns 2).

what: Empty --only and non-positive --smallest selected the wrong population (everything, or all but the largest).
how: main() refuses rc 2 before the halt check or any work when --only is given with no names or --smallest <= 0; the filters now test 'is not None'.

what: drift() counted non-dict entries that rebuild() skips, and one odd evidence field aborted the whole rebuild.
how: drift() counts dict entries only; the per-file evidence row build is wrapped so a bad chars_read or provenance names the file in unreadable_evidence and continues. Not reproduced as a traceback by the audit; reproduced here.

what: subsystem_stopped read a falsy STOPPED.json row as not stopped while truthy non-dict rows raised.
how: Presence of the key means stopped: absent name is not stopped; any present row that is not a dict (null, empty, false, list, string) reports stopped with a reason. Fail-closed for every malformed shape.

what: sweep.py, worldseed --write and corpus_db --rebuild write derived outputs but are not on _INTERLOCKED and do not call assert_clear.
how: Options: (a) add all three to the interlock roster with assert_clear in their write paths (needs a verify_math.py roster edit, which is not mine); (b) rule that derived outputs are exempt and record that in the 2026-09-28 ruling. Owner ruling needed on whether 'twenty' was meant to exclude derived files.

what: register() read-modify-writes WIKI_HOSTS.json with write_json and no compare-and-swap, unlike hostcheck._land_hosts.
how: Options: switch to the same digest-then-replace_if_unchanged loop hostcheck uses (small, but it changes the write path of a not-reconstructible file), or leave it as a hand-run tool. Needs a ruling on whether hand-run tools are exempt from the CAS rule.

what: A synthesis whose best band is 'unassayed' is merged and the source then drops out of stranded_sources() with no ceiling and no band.
how: Parity with pipeline.phase_synthesis. Options: leave (terminal state by design), or list unassayed-band syntheses as outstanding in stranded_sources(). Curatorial ruling needed on the intended terminal state.

what: known_present_titles draws canary titles from excluded (struck) entries (sweep67 b14 Q5), and tuning.py POOL_PROOF staleness (b04 Q5) also stands.
how: Unchanged and still open. binding_health: skip entries with excluded set when choosing canary titles (small) but that changes which titles the canary probes. tuning: needs a ruling on how much weight a stale POOL_PROOF should carry. Not fixed without that.
